transport: VE.Can on RJ45 per the product line, plus Bluetooth. Neither bit rate, node address, nor register set is stated for this model in any committed document.
gotchas: Recorded so nobody researches it twice. docs/victron-ve-can-registers-v20.pdf names "Lynx Ion" for four messages — a predecessor product — and never names the Lynx Smart BMS or the NG generation. Version 20 of that document is old enough that an "NG" model cannot be assumed into it.

The one piece of protocol evidence that touches this product line is the BLE side: extra-manufacturer-data record type 0x0A is literally titled "(Lynx Smart) BMS" and its layout is fully specified. That is the `victron-ble-lynx-bms-record-0a` entry above, and even there the model binding is unverified because the 2022

The retail listing claims Bluetooth and VRM and does not name a protocol. VRM is Victron's cloud and reaches the device through a GX, not directly — that route is `victron-gx-modbus-tcp` in docs/catalog/lan-http.md, and it changes the question from "what does this BMS speak" to "what does the GX expose about it".

A BMS is the one device class where getting the map wrong is not just a wasted afternoon: allowed-to-charge and allowed-to-discharge are the fields a rules engine would act on, and no committed document states where they live for this model.
